statements.status_notes: CVE-2012-0039: g_str_hash in GLib is the unseeded djb hash, so an attacker who controls the strings an application stores in a GHashTable keyed with g_str_hash can choose colliding keys and make lookups slow, a CPU denial of service (http://openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2012/01/10/12, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=772720). The CVE record is tagged disputed: the GLib maintainer's position, in that Red Hat bug, is that g_str_hash is documented API that cannot change and that every GHashTable user chooses its own hash function. Debian lists the issue as unfixed in every release and rates it unimportant (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2012-0039, Debian bug 655044), while Red Hat rates it Moderate and affected. This owner ships Debian's glib2.0 2.84.4, whose g_str_hash (glib/ghash.c) is still that unseeded hash, so the behaviour is present in every published build. Pending: a maintainer decision on whether to adopt the upstream position, that the exposure belongs to applications that hash untrusted keys with g_str_hash, as not affected for every image built on this owner, given that Red Hat still rates it affected.
